editorial:
Imagine being left for dead by the person you trusted most in the world. That is exactly where you find yourself when you meet Medea. She is a powerful queen who gave up everything for her husband, Jason, only for him to dump her so he could marry a younger princess for more power. You can feel her anger building up from the very first scene. The vibe is heavy and tense, focusing more on the emotional war between a husband and wife than on big action scenes. It feels like a stage play brought to life, where every word spoken is like a slap in the face.

What really makes this work is the acting; the lead actress makes you feel both sorry for her and scared of her at the same time. The pacing is a bit slow because it is an old TV movie, but the drama keeps you locked in. If you like stories about betrayal and revenge, you should definitely give this a try. Since it is an older title, you might have to hunt for a digital rental on Apple TV or look for a restored version to add to your physical Blu-ray collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The story ends in a shocking way. To get the ultimate revenge on Jason, Medea decides to kill their own children. She knows this will hurt him more than anything else. After she commits this terrible act, she does not stay to face the music. Instead, she escapes in a flying chariot sent by her grandfather. Jason is left completely broken and alone, losing his new bride, his kids, and his pride all at once.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic plays and stories about revenge.
